title: Vibrating Feeder

introduction.definition: A vibrating feeder moves bulk material along a tray by vibration. Two unbalanced (exciter) motors turn in opposite directions; their forces cancel sideways and add in one direction, so the tray moves along a straight line at an angle. Each stroke throws the particles slightly up and forward, so the material "hops" along. Springs isolate the vibrating tray from the hopper support.
applications: Feeding crushers, screens and conveyors from hoppers
Controlled feeding of aggregates, coal, ore, food products
key_points: Linear motion from twin counter-rotating exciters
Feed rate set by amplitude and frequency (VFD)
No moving parts in contact with material except the liner
introduction.summary: A vibrating feeder moves bulk material by vibrating a tray. Two counter-rotating unbalanced motors create a straight-line vibration at an angle; each stroke throws the particles slightly forward and up, so they hop along the tray at a rate set by amplitude and frequency.

foundation: Support on steelwork or a concrete plinth designed for the hopper/bin load on the feeder plus impact and dynamic loads.
Isolate vibrating machines from the structure with their springs/rubber mounts — never weld or rigidly bolt the vibrating body to the structure.
alignment: Set the feeder at the designed slope and centre it under the hopper outlet; set skirt boards and the hopper gate to the design bed depth.
Align drive and driven shafts (laser or dial gauge) or set the exciter motors as the maker specifies.
piping: Chutes and skirts: allow a gap that widens in the direction of travel so material does not jam; fit dust seals and connect dust extraction where required.
Leave clear access for liner change and for the hopper shut-off gate.
commissioning: Run empty first: check direction, amplitude/speed, temperatures and noise.
Load gradually, check the material bed is even and the discharge rate matches the set-point; record motor current as a baseline.

routine.task: Check feed, noise and that the tray is free (no contact with chutes).

periodic.task: Inspect springs and liners; check exciter bolts and weight settings.

overhaul.task: Replace exciter bearings, liners and springs as needed.

lubrication: Bearings: grease or oil to the maker's schedule and quantity — do not over-grease vibrating-machine bearings (heat).

symptoms: Feed rate drops, material builds up
remedies: Clean liners; check eccentric weights and spring condition

causes: Fatigue from long running at high amplitude
remedies: Repair to maker's procedure; check amplitude and isolators

safety: Lock out exciter motors; beware stored energy in springs and hanging material in the hopper.

video_tutorials.title: Vibrating Feeder — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Vibrating Feeder.
A vibrating feeder moves bulk material along a tray by vibration.
Two unbalanced (exciter) motors turn in opposite directions; their forces cancel sideways and add in one direction, so the tray moves along a straight line at an angle.
Each stroke throws the particles slightly up and forward, so the material "hops" along.
Typical applications include feeding crushers, screens and conveyors from hoppers; controlled feeding of aggregates, coal, ore, food products; batching and dosing (variable frequency).

script.narration: How the Vibrating Feeder works.
Material from the hopper rests on the tray.
The counter-rotating exciters create a straight-line vibration at about 30° to the tray.
Each stroke throws particles up and forward, so they progress along the tray.
Coil springs isolate the tray from the support so little vibration reaches the structure.

video_tutorials.title: Vibrating Feeder — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Vibrating Feeder.
Check feed, noise and that the tray is free (no contact with chutes).
Inspect springs and liners; check exciter bolts and weight settings.
Replace exciter bearings, liners and springs as needed.
Watch for uneven or reduced feed: feed rate drops, material builds up. Common cause: sticky material.
Watch for cracks in tray or body: visible cracks near stiffeners. Common cause: fatigue from long running at high amplitude.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: How do two counter-rotating exciters produce straight-line vibration?
options: Their forces add in all directions
Sideways components cancel, components along one line add

questions.question: How is feed rate commonly adjusted?
options: Vary frequency (VFD) or exciter weight setting
questions.explanation: Amplitude and frequency set the rate.

questions.question: Which component has this function? "Carries and conveys material."
questions.explanation: Feeder Tray (pan) with Liners: Carries and conveys material.

questions.question: Which component has this function? "Generate the vibration."
questions.explanation: Twin Unbalanced-Motor Exciters (counter-rotating → straight-line vibration): Generate the vibration.

questions.question: Which component has this function? "Isolate vibration from the structure."
questions.explanation: Coil-Spring Isolators: Isolate vibration from the structure.
